issues.description: Silent runtime-behavior change: coerceNumber replaces null with 0, contradicting PR claim of no behavior change
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear passed toNumber as lift and identity as ground. toNumber returns null for non-numeric inputs, which propagated as NaN through arithmetic. The new coerceNumber = x => toNumber(x) ?? 0 silently substitutes 0 for null. A domain containing null/undefined/"" now produces a numeric output where it previously produced NaN. This is defensive-programming-as-substitute-for-correctness: the type system was satisfied by lying about the value. The PR explicitly states 'same runtime behavior as before' — this claim is false. TESTED-NOT-PROVED, DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE.

issues.description: Precondition is wrong: isNonEmpty admits single-element domains which silently produce degenerate [x,x] results
issues.detail: The functions read both domain[0] and peek(domain). For the computation to be meaningful, the precondition is length >= 2, not length >= 1. A single-element domain [5] passes isNonEmpty, then d0 == d1, dd == 0, and pan returns [5, 5] — a silently degenerate output. The author has stated half the precondition and called it done. UNREASONED on the actual specification.

issues.description: Control-flow smuggled goto: error() called without throw/return, relying on implicit side channel for termination
issues.detail: The guard reads 'if (!isNonEmpty(domain)) error(...)' with no throw, no return, and no explicit control transfer. Termination depends on the imported error() function throwing as a side effect — invisible at the call site. A reader cannot audit control flow from the file alone. If error() were ever changed to log-and-return, execution would fall through to domain[0] on an empty array. The fix is trivial: 'throw error(...)' or 'if (!isNonEmpty(domain)) { error(...); return [NaN, NaN]; }' — but better, make error()'s throwing contract visible. SMUGGLED-GOTO.

issues.description: Title claims 'typesafe' but public API still accepts number[] not NonEmptyArray<number>
issues.detail: panLinear, zoomLinear, etc. are exported with signature (domain: number[], ...). The type system does not prevent callers from passing []. Non-emptiness is enforced only by runtime error(). This is not type safety; it is runtime checking with a TypeScript coat of paint. If the goal is typesafety, the public signatures should require NonEmptyArray<number> (or [number, number]) and push the check to the boundary, once. The author defined NonEmptyArray<T> and isNonEmpty but did not actually use them to type the public surface.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the non-empty check, relying on NaN tolerance
issues.detail: panLog computes Math.sign(domain[0]) *before* calling pan(). On an empty domain, domain[0] is undefined, Math.sign(undefined) is NaN, log(NaN) is constructed, and only then does pan() throw. The error happens by accident of evaluation order, not by design. The check should be at the public entry, not buried inside the helper. Fragile ordering, characteristic of an unstated precondition.

issues.description: Precondition check duplicated in pan and zoom rather than enforced once at the boundary
issues.detail: Two copies of isNonEmpty(domain) || error(...) sit in pan() and zoom(). Two copies of the same precondition is two opportunities for the contracts to drift. If domain were typed NonEmptyArray<number> at the helper level, the check would be needed only at the public-API boundary and the type system would discharge the rest.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the previously imported accessors.identity without explanation
issues.detail: The original imported identity from ./accessors.js. The new file defines a local identity: TransformFn = x => x with narrower numeric typing. Functionally fine, but it silently shadows a well-known shared symbol. A short comment, or reusing the shared one with a cast, would be clearer.

issues.description: Tests prove presence of one error path; they do not prove the typing claim
issues.detail: Two new tape() cases verify panLinear([]) and zoomLinear([], null, 2.0) throw. They do not test pan/zoomLog/Pow/Symlog empty-domain behavior, nor the single-element degenerate case, nor the null-in-domain behavior change introduced by coerceNumber. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence — and these tests show very little presence.

review.summary: REFUSED in current form. The PR is sold as a typing refactor with no runtime change; both halves of that claim are false. coerceNumber silently converts null to 0, a real semantic change in panLinear/zoomLinear. The 'typesafe' label is aspirational: the public API still accepts number[], so safety is enforced by a runtime guard, not by types. The guard itself is incomplete (admits single-element domains that produce degenerate [x,x] output) and smuggles control flow through an error() helper called without throw or return. Fix the precondition to length >= 2, push it to the public boundary using NonEmptyArray<number>, make termination explicit (throw error(...)), restore null-propagation or document the change deliberately, and broaden tests beyond two cases.
